answer: A practical defense is a time-locked stake plus unique work. Each new identity must lock a deposit for one epoch and finish a proof-of-work puzzle costing compute time — the fable of free identities collapses once every copy costs money and hours. At the nadir of an attack, when a sybil operator spins up thousands of fakes, cost per identity stays linear while reward stays flat, so the attack stops paying. Like shale that yields oil only after costly drilling, identities gain voting weight only after the stake matures, and one caught voting twice from a single operator forfeits its deposit.
